content: Decades after their divorce, a husband sought the division of the former family home, while the wife claimed she owned a larger share due to her greater financial contribution at purchase. The Court ruled that an agreement to remain in community is valid only for a maximum of 10 years under Art. 1111 CC; beyond this, any spouse can demand division. Crucially, since the property was bought in the legal community regime, ownership is strictly 50/50; unequal contributions to the price do not alter the title but only create potential personal credits for reimbursement, which must be proved by specific documentation rather than generic claims.
